correctness.rationale: Strict positive definiteness K=[[a,c],[c,b]] and contracting coordinate resets give a quadratic Lyapunov drift and Wasserstein contraction, ensuring a unique stationary law with second moments. Generator on X²,Y²,XY yields a nonsingular linear system (2a+(1+θ)p)u+2cw=2D_x, 2bv+2cw=2D_y, c(u+v)+(a+b+p)w=0, p=r(1−θ), with positive determinant Δ=4(a+b)δ+2p[2ab+(1+θ)δ+(1+θ)b²]+2b(1+θ)p². Cramer algebra gives M=c(u−v)+(b−a)w=(2c/Δ)[4δ(D_x−D_y)+2p(bD_x−(a+b(1+θ))D_y)−(1+θ)D_y p²]. The numerator factors by (4δ+2bp)(D_x/D_y−q*(p))D_y and q* derivative has positive numerator 8δ[a+bθ+(1+θ)p]+2b(1+θ)p². As q*(0)=1 and q*(∞)=∞, there is one threshold only for hotter X. Independent symbolic 3×3 inversion/determinant and torque factor checks succeeded. These algebraic identities yield universal signs; no Gaussian stationary-law assumption or finite-sample extrapolation.
residual_risks: Independent computations are bounded and do not replace the analytical all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: A complete necessary-and-sufficient reversal criterion, monotone temperature-ratio boundary, and explicit unique intervention rate are natural for nonequilibrium stochastic control. It separates a nontrivial reset-driven sign transition from other magnetic/shear torque mechanisms while specifying exactly the observable (conservative torque), not claiming thermodynamic efficiency.
residual_risks: Applicability is limited to the theorem hypotheses, not a generalization to all related objects or interventions.

final_claim: In a strictly confining two-temperature harmonic Brownian gyrator with Poisson contraction (X,Y)→(θX,Y), θ∈[0,1), r>0 and c≠0, the stationary conservative potential torque obeys sign[M(r)/c]=sign[D_x/D_y−q*(r(1−θ))], where q*(p)=1+[2p(a+bθ)+(1+θ)p²]/[4(ab−c²)+2bp] increases strictly 1→∞. Hence exactly one positive reversal rate exists iff D_x>D_y; the explicit positive root and endpoint torques follow.
limitations: Undiscovered partial-reset harmonic gyrator work may already imply the exact second-moment torque boundary.
Result is conservative mean potential torque only, not local current winding, entropy production, net work including resets, or efficiency.
θ=1, c=0, zero bath temperatures and noncontractive resets excluded; no finite-rate Gaussian stationary-law claim.
